programmes.funder: BioInnovation Institute (funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation)
programmes.amount_note: Up to DKK 5.35M (about EUR 0.72M) per year for up to three years, plus in-kind support.
programmes.deadline_note: Challenge calls twice a year; expected deadlines May and December (current call labelled 'Open Call' on bii.dk home page).

eligibility.other_note: For Principal Investigators with at least 3 years' experience as independent group leader; PI stays at home institution, project team hired at BII in Copenhagen. Existing IP not required.

programmes.source_snippet: translating their science into innovative products and solutions

programmes.funder: BioInnovation Institute in partnership with NATO DIANA
programmes.amount_note: Contractual funding of EUR 100,000 for a 6-month NATO DIANA programme run by BII (selection is made by DIANA HQ).
programmes.deadline_note: Deadline for the 2027 NATO DIANA cohort was 3 July 2026 13:00 CEST; next cohort deadline not yet published.

eligibility.other_note: Company must be headquartered in a NATO country, work in one of the nine NATO Emerging and Disruptive Technology areas with dual-use potential and address a DIANA challenge.

programmes.funder: BioInnovation Institute (funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation)
programmes.amount_note: DKK 4.2M convertible loan (12 months, Danish-incorporated start-ups with no commercial investors); the separate International Venture Lab offers up to EUR 500,000 convertible loan.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications assessed in evaluation rounds; the International Venture Lab states next evaluation 16 Dec 2026 (pre-application by 24 Oct, full application by 30 Oct 2026). No fixed deadline published for the Danish Venture Lab block.

eligibility.other_note: Evidence-based idea and founder team; Danish Venture Lab only supports early-stage companies without commercial investments/ownership; company must be incorporated and led from Denmark on acceptance.

programmes.source_snippet: Helps early-stage start-ups accelerate their journey towards validated venture

programmes.amount_note: The Game Funding Scheme (now run by NIMBI) provides DKK 15 million per year for development, production and launch of Danish digital games; development grants up to or over DKK 100,000, production and launch grants.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 application deadlines listed: 22 January and 1 September 2026 (both passed). Grants before 2025 were administered by the Danish Film Institute.

eligibility.other_note: Applicant must be affiliated with a company that develops, produces and launches Danish digital games and is based in Denmark, an EU/EEA state or Switzerland.

programmes.amount_note: Growth loan for SMEs that cannot obtain full bank financing; amount and terms set case by case.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; EIFO offers loans and guarantees directly or together with the company's bank. A dedicated 'Vaekstlaan' product page was not found, so terms are not confirmed.

programmes.amount_note: Direct equity and fund-of-funds investment in Danish tech companies; ticket size set case by case, normally alongside private investors.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; EIFO invests as an active minority shareholder on market terms, typically alongside funds, business angels or industrial partners.

programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA) with the national space agency or regional co-funder
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50,000 equity-free funding for product and IP development, plus up to two years of incubation with technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal and IPR advice and fundraising support. Some national BICs add local top-up funding.
programmes.deadline_note: This ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. Contact the local centre for the next deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the local ESA BIC to discuss suitability
Submit application documents before the local deadline
Tender Opening Board review, then presentation to the Tender Evaluation Board
Register a company in Denmark before signing the incubation contract

eligibility.other_note: Business must use space-based systems, apply space technology in a non-space domain, or develop products and services for the space sector. Company must be registered in Denmark.

programmes.source_snippet: €50k equity free funding for product and IP development

programmes.name_en: Danish Energy Technology Development and Demonstration Programme
programmes.amount_note: Grants for development and demonstration of new energy technology. Support intensity depends on company size and project type under EU state aid rules; project grants commonly range from a few million to over one hundred million DKK.
programmes.deadline_note: EUDP runs two rounds a year (2025-II, 2026-I with deadline 25 Feb 2026). The latest round has closed (79 applications for DKK 772 million received); the next call is not yet announced. The old ens.dk page no longer exists.

eligibility.other_note: Danish-registered entity required; foreign partners can participate in the consortium.

programmes.amount_note: DKK 5-40 million investment depending on the call; up to 75% of total project budget (90% for quantum technology).
programmes.deadline_note: No call currently available on 2026-10-05; two-phase process (Letter of Interest, then full application), about 9 months overall.

eligibility.other_note: Danish and international organisations can take part but the lead applicant must be Danish; collaboration between companies, research institutions and public organisations.

programmes.amount_note: Apply for DKK 200,000–5,000,000. The fund covers a maximum of 35% of total project costs; the company funds the rest.
programmes.deadline_note: Pool 4 (Innobooster 4th call 2026) is open 20 Aug - 15 Oct 2026 (12:00); decisions expected 8-26 Feb 2027. Later pools follow throughout the year.
programmes.reopen_note: Next window opens 20 August 2026 and closes 15 October 2026 (period 4 of 2026).

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility (SME, capital or gross-profit criterion)
Prepare the project description and budget on Innovationsfonden's templates
Submit via the fund's application portal within an open window
Assessment on idea quality, impact and execution quality

documents_required.doc: Documentation of capital raised or gross profit

eligibility.other_note: Danish CVR-registered SME; needs either at least DKK 100,000 of risk capital/development grants in the past three years or gross profit of at least DKK 250,000 in one of the last three years. Themes include green, life science, critical and digital technologies, and defence and security.

programmes.source_snippet: Applicants can apply for between DKK 200,000 and DKK 5 million, and the fund covers a maximum of 35% of a project's total costs.

programmes.amount_note: DKK 500,000 - 1.5 million (including overhead) for a project of up to 12 months; paid to the applicant's institution.

eligibility.other_note: For employees at Danish public research and educational institutions and hospitals who want to turn research results into a business; the institution must be involved. Not open to companies directly.

programmes.amount_note: DKK 27,500 per founder per month for the 12-month programme plus a development grant of up to DKK 100,000 (maximum for one founder about DKK 430,000).

eligibility.other_note: Individual or team of up to three founders; each founder needs at least 120 ECTS of higher education, owns at least 12.5% of the company, works at least 37 hours per week and has no more than 10 hours of other work/education; company must have a Danish CVR before the programme starts.

programmes.amount_note: Researchers and companies can have compounds screened free of charge in LEO Pharma's dermatology assays and retain full rights to their compounds and any resulting data.
programmes.deadline_note: The old openinnovation.leo-pharma.com portal now redirects to leo-pharma.com. LEO Pharma invites partnership enquiries in medical dermatology via its business development team; there are no fixed calls or grants.

eligibility.other_note: Dermatology focus; open to academic researchers and companies worldwide. Screening is in-kind, not cash.

programmes.name_local: Novo Nordisk Fonden - Innovation og tidlig kommercialisering
programmes.name_en: Novo Nordisk Foundation - Innovation and early commercialisation grants
programmes.amount_note: Pioneer Innovator Grant: up to DKK 1.2 million per grant for 1 year (total budget DKK 190 million per year for Pioneer and Distinguished Innovator grants).
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call opened 1 Aug and closed 15 Sep 2026 14:00 (Copenhagen); results December 2026.

eligibility.other_note: Main applicant must be a researcher or student employed at a university, hospital or research institution in the Nordic countries; grants cannot be given to a company (pre-CVR).

programmes.source_snippet: support for projects in open competition and for stand-alone initiatives

programmes.amount_note: Innovation Fund Denmark co-funding of up to EUR 500,000 per project in total and EUR 50,000-300,000 per Danish partner; funding rate 35-90% of costs for each participant depending on the call.
programmes.deadline_note: IFD's 2026 plan lists Eurostars 3 Call 10 (deadline 19 March 2026) and Call 11 'to be announced'; no open deadline published at verification.

eligibility.other_note: R&D-performing SMEs in Denmark with international consortium partners from at least one other Eurostars country; partners may include large companies, universities and research organisations.

programmes.source_snippet: It is the largest international funding programme for SMEs wishing to collaborate with partners (large companies, universities, research organizations etc.) on R&D projects that create innovative products, processes or services for commercialisation.

programmes.name_local: Industrial PhD in the private sector
programmes.amount_note: Up to DKK 17,000 per month towards the Industrial PhD student's salary, up to DKK 100,000 towards the company's travel and course costs, and a fixed DKK 360,000 (incl. overhead) for the university.
programmes.deadline_note: Autumn 2026 round was open 4 Aug 2026 - 8 Sep 2026 at 12:00; IFD expects a spring round in January-February (see programme page).
programmes.reopen_note: Next round expected early 2027; check Industrial Researcher programme page.

eligibility.other_note: Private company with activities in Denmark, a university partner and an Industrial PhD student; business-oriented research project.

programmes.source_snippet: Collaboration between a private company in Denmark, a university and an Industrial PhD student.

programmes.name_local: Industrial Postdoc in the private sector
programmes.amount_note: Company grant of DKK 712,000 (DKK 612,000 salary contribution at DKK 22,000 per month plus DKK 100,000 for travel); the university receives a separate grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Application windows set per round (Industrial PhD and postdoc rounds expected January-February and August-September); no open deadline confirmed on 2026-10-05.

eligibility.other_note: Danish private company collaborating with a university to employ a researcher who already holds a PhD.

programmes.source_snippet: Industrial Postdoc for researchers who already have a PhD.

programmes.name_en: Innowwide market feasibility call (Innovation Fund Denmark)
programmes.amount_note: Co-funding for a six-month market feasibility project with an independent subcontractor in a target market; eligible project costs must be at least EUR 86,000 and include subcontracting costs.
programmes.reopen_note: Check IFD site for the next Innowwide call.

eligibility.other_note: SME applicant; project must involve an independent subcontractor in the target country and focus exclusively on civilian applications.

programmes.source_snippet: SMEs can carry out a market feasibility project at different stages—for example, when exploring or developing a research and development (R&D) idea, or after a successful R&D project to assess whether their new product, process or service can be commercialised in selected global markets.

programmes.name_en: EIFO Ukraine Facility (loans and guarantees for Danish exporters)
programmes.amount_note: Loan and guarantee facility with total capacity of DKK 7.15 billion: financing to Ukrainian buyers (direct EIFO loans or 100% risk cover of bank and exporter credit), grants covering up to 40% of the financing need for public buyers, and risk cover of Danish exporters' investments and contracts.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling expressions of interest, assessed at monthly screening committee meetings (ukrainefond@eifo.dk).

eligibility.other_note: Danish exporters, Ukrainian buyers and banks; project must contain at least 30% Danish economic interest; buyer equity at least three times the loan; buyer must show audited accounts for five years.

programmes.source_snippet: Danske eksportører kan søge om lån og garantier fra Ukraine-faciliteten.
